families.title: Crates
families.summary: Stackable crates and caps from 1x1 to 3x2 grid units: the base every other part fits.
families.description:
The base range: plain stackable crates and caps in the sizes people actually print.

Exported sizes: crates 1x1x3, 2x1x3, 2x2x3, 2x2x6 and 3x2x6; caps 1x1, 2x1, 2x2 and 3x2.
Any other size from 1x1x2 to 8x8x40 comes from the CLI, e.g. `uv run stakee box 4x2x6`.

Size: a crate of `nx x ny x h` units is `42 * n - 0.5` mm per side and `7 * h + 4` mm
tall to the top of its stacking lip. The usable cavity is `42 * n - 4.5` mm per side and
`7 * h - 5.5` mm deep, measured from the floor to the stacking seat.

Stacking: the Gridfinity-profile feet of an upper crate drop into the lip of the crate below
and seat on its 45 deg chamfers, so the upper crate stands at exactly `z = 7 * h` of the
lower one, with a 0.75 mm shadow gap between the bodies. `verify()` checks this for every
exported size: a box and a cap placed at `7 * h` overlap the crate by zero volume, and
collide with it when lowered 0.05 mm (they seat on the chamfers, they do not hover).

Caps (`make_cap`): one hollow foot plus a 2.4 mm top plate, 7.15 mm tall. A cap seats in
the lip of any crate with the same footprint. Its top is flat, so it ends the stack.

Features of every crate (all from `make_box` in `stakee/core.py`):

- Magnet pockets: four per grid cell under the feet, 6.5 mm wide and 2.4 mm deep, 13 mm
  from the cell center on both axes, for optional 6x2 mm disc magnets.
- Divider slots: 1.6 mm wide and 0.8 mm deep, every 21 mm on all four inner walls. They run
  from the floor up through the lip, so a plate drops straight in. They take the 1.2 mm
  plates and 1.5 mm thick ends of the `dividers` family.
- Label recess: on the front (-Y) face, `min(width - 16, 60)` mm wide, 12 mm tall and
  0.6 mm deep, its top 1.5 mm below the stacking seat. Crates under 3 units tall have none.
  Caps carry the same recess on top.
- Clip sockets: eight L-shaped bayonet pockets on the side (+/-X) faces, 12 mm in from the
  front and back faces. Each side has two centered 2 mm below the lip top and two centered
  6.5 mm above the bottom. The `kit` stack clip locks two stacked crates together through them.

families.title: Dividers
families.summary: Interlocking X/Y rails, hook-on plates and bridges that split a crate; all print flat.
families.description:
Modular dividers: interlocking rails plus short hook-on plates, all printed flat.

System:
- Rails span the whole cavity and sit in the core wall slots (every 21 mm). An X rail
  (running along X) is notched from the bottom, a Y rail from the top, so any X and Y
  rails cross like an egg crate. Rail ends are 1.5 mm thick in the 1.6 mm slot: they
  stay put but slide out by hand.
- Hook plates start in a wall slot and hang on an X rail with a hook over its top edge,
  anywhere along it. Bridges hang between two X rails.
- Hooks only go on X rails: a Y rail has notches in its top edge at every slot.

Every part is a profile in its local XZ plane, extruded through its thickness, so it
prints flat with no supports. Local Y spans [-0.75, 0.45] (plate) and [-0.75, 0.75]
(thick ends), so a part laid on its -Y face sits flat on the bed.

families.title: Inserts
families.summary: Drop-in trays that turn a crate into a kit: dev-board dock, solder station, parts grid.
families.description:
Drop-in inserts: trays that sit on a crate floor and turn a generic crate into a kit.

Every insert is modelled in its own frame (centered on XY, bottom at z = 0) and is
meant to sit at z = FLOOR_Z inside the crate it names. Inserts keep CLEARANCE per side
to the cavity walls and stay below the stacking seat (`size.lip_top - SEAT_DEPTH`),
so a crate or cap still stacks on top.

families.title: Bag Library
families.summary: A tall crate that files distributor zip bags upright like a card index, with tab cards.
families.description:
Bag Library: file distributor zip bags upright like a card index, labels facing up and out.

A tall crate sized from `BoxSize.cavity` so a bag stands on its short edge and still clears
a cap, a thumb window in the front wall below the label/seat band, slot-keyed index cards with
staggered embossed tabs, and a sliding follower that props up a half-empty row.

families.title: Drawer cabinet
families.summary: Stackable sleeves with an open front and the drawers that slide into them.
families.description:
Drawer cabinet: stackable sleeves with an open front, and the drawers that slide into them.

A sleeve keeps the whole crate contract (core feet underneath, core lip pocket on top, clip
sockets on the sides), so sleeves stack on each other at exactly 7 * h, sit on Gridfinity
baseplates and on any crate of the same footprint, and take a crate or a cap on top. Its front
wall is cut away below a lintel; a stack of sleeves is the cabinet.

Frames: a sleeve is centered on XY with its feet on z = 0 (front face -Y). A drawer is exported
in the frame of its sleeve, lowered by FLOOR_Z: placed at (0, 0, FLOOR_Z) it is closed.

Mechanism, all in the printed geometry (no hardware):
- Closing stop: the front plate is wider and taller than the opening; its back face lands on
  the sleeve's front face (side walls and lintel). The tray keeps BACK_CLEARANCE to the back.
- Retention stop: a 1 mm block on the sleeve floor, just behind the front wall, runs in a
  groove under the drawer floor. A catch in the groove meets it after TRAVEL mm. The catch is
  rigid: lift the drawer front (it tilts about its back edge, the lintel leaves TOP_CLEARANCE)
  and the catch rises over the block, so the drawer comes out; pushing it back in, the 45 deg
  ramp behind the catch lifts it the same way.
- Closed detent: two tongues cut free in the drawer side walls carry 45 deg bumps that click
  into vertical dimples in the sleeve walls when the drawer is closed. They only rub for the
  first few mm of travel, then leave the sleeve.

Print: sleeves upright on their feet; the lintel is the only bridge (as wide as the cavity).
Drawers upright on their floor; the groove under the floor bridges GROOVE_WIDTH. No supports.

families.title: Pocket box
families.summary: A small hinged, latched box to carry around that still stacks like a crate.
families.description:
Pocket box: a small hinged, latched box you carry, that is still a Stakee box.

Closed, base + lid have the envelope of a `BoxSize(nx, ny, 4)` crate: Gridfinity feet under
the base, a full stacking lip on top of the lid at `7 * h + 4`. So the closed box seats on
any crate's lip at `7 * h_lower` and a crate or cap seats on it at `7 * h`.

Parting plane `z = split`: the base is the core crate cut there; the lid is a solid slab
(printed on its flat underside) with the core lip pocket and a floor `STACK_CLEARANCE` below
the feet of whatever stacks on it.

Hinge (back, along X): a pin hinge for a length of 1.75 mm filament. The axis lies
`KNUCKLE_R` in from the back face and `KNUCKLE_R` above the parting plane, so every knuckle
stays inside the footprint and the lid's knuckles touch the bed. Five knuckles alternate base /
lid / base / lid / base. Behind the axis the lid only keeps material above a 45 deg chord (inside
the knuckle radius, so it turns in place), and the base is recessed behind the axis down to
`RECESS_BELOW_AXIS` under it: a lid point can only swing back into the footprint if it lies
within `KNUCKLE_R / cos(angle / 2)` of the axis, so the recess sets the opening angle; at
about 120 deg the lid's back rests on the recess floor.

Latch (front, center): a cantilever tab grown from the base inside a front pocket, flush with
the front face. Its inward bump clicks into a notch in the lid's front slot; the bump's flat
underside holds the lid shut, its 45 deg top lets the lid push it aside when closing. To open,
pull the tab top toward you by the nail groove (1.1 mm at the bump) and lift.

families.title: Carry kit
families.summary: Stack clip, tote handle cap, NFC label cap and tool-rack cap for a grab-and-go stack.
families.description:
Grab-and-go kit: accessories that turn a stack of crates into a carryable hacker kit.

Parts: a bayonet stack clip that locks two stacked crates together at the seam, a tote handle
cap, an NFC label cap with a swappable snap-in text tile, and a tool rack cap.

Clip geometry is expressed relative to the seam `z = 7 * h_lower` (the stacking pitch):
the lower crate's lip socket sits at `LIP_ABOVE_NOMINAL - CLIP_SOCKET_LIP_Z` = +2.0 mm and
the upper part's base socket at `CLIP_SOCKET_BASE_Z` = +6.5 mm, for every box height.
The sockets are core's L pockets: the clip's L nubs go into the windows, then the clip slides
`CLIP_SOCKET_LEG` along the face so the hooks sit behind the skin.

families.title: Magnetic tray
families.summary: A stackable screw tray with hidden magnets and one numbered compartment per step.
families.description:
Magnetic repair tray: a 1-unit stackable cap whose top is a numbered screw tray.

Design: the tray side is the top, so it never has to be flipped (a flipped tray would pour
its screws out). The underside is the solid cap foot (same envelope as `make_cap`), so it
seats in any crate's stacking lip at `z = 7 * h`. The rim is a full stacking lip at the
1-unit height (lip top 11 mm, like a `BoxSize(nx, ny, 1)`), so crates and caps stack on
top of it at a 7 mm pitch: put the tray on a crate mid-repair, stack the next crate on it,
and the screws stay put underneath. On the bench it stands on its flat foot.

Each compartment (one per disassembly step, debossed step number in the back-left corner)
has filleted floor edges and one 10x2 mm N52 disc magnet at its center, sealed in by a print
pause under a 0.6 mm ceiling (3 layers at 0.2 mm). Divider tops stop 0.2 mm below the feet
of a crate stacked on top; screws lying flat (M2.5 head <= 2.5 mm) clear those feet.

families.title: ESD crates
families.summary: Crates with a ground point (banana socket or snap stud) for dissipative filament.
families.description:
ESD crates: the standard Stakee crate with a ground point, for static-dissipative filament.

The ground point is a 6.5 mm through hole in the back (+Y) wall, backed by a pad on the inside
that makes the wall 6 mm thick there and carries a flat-top hex pocket for the nut. It takes
either hardware option, both of which clamp metal against the printed wall from both sides:

- a 4 mm banana socket with an M6 threaded body (the common panel-mount type, e.g. Electro-PJP
  3240 / 3115: M6 stud, 10 mm A/F nut): collar outside, nut captive in the hex pocket, so it
  tightens from outside with a spanner on the collar. Sockets made for an 8 mm hole (e.g. PJP
  3230) fit after drilling the hole out to 8 mm; their nut then bears on the pad face.
- a 10 mm male snap stud (the ESD wrist-strap / mat-cord snap) with a screw post or centre
  hole: M3 or M4 screw through the hole, DIN 125 washer (9 mm OD) + nut in the hex pocket.

Location: centre x = GRID / 4 (10.5 mm), midway between the divider slots at x = 0 and 21 for
every footprint width, hole centre 12.75 mm above the bottom. That keeps the 18 mm pad 0.9 mm
clear of both neighbouring divider plates, below the stacking seat (pad top 20.0 mm vs seat
>= 21.0 mm), and the 14 mm outside clamp face away from clip sockets (+/-X) and label (-Y).

Stacked crates touch only through the feet resting in the lip. Printed-surface to
printed-surface contact resistance is high and unpredictable, so do not count on a stack
grounding itself: give every crate its own lead, or chain the jacks with banana leads.

families.title: Wire dispenser
families.summary: A crate with a lift-out axle and one eyelet per spool for hookup wire.
families.description:
Wire dispenser: a crate that holds hookup-wire spools on an axle, with one eyelet per spool.

Pull the colour you need through its eyelet in the front (-Y) wall; the spools spin
independently on a lift-out axle, so nothing tangles.

Parts: the crate (core box + eyelet ledge + eyelets + optional snip slot), a drop-in cradle
frame with two open-top U-cradles, a printed axle (or an 8 mm steel / M8 threaded rod) and
spacer washers. Everything is parametric in `SpoolSpec`; the footprint and height are
the smallest that fit, so `uv run python -m stakee.modules.wirespool` re-plans the whole
dispenser for your spools once you edit `DEFAULT_SPOOLS`.

Default spools: the common 6-colour 22 AWG kits (TUOFENG, Etokfoks...) ship six 9 m spools
in a ~145 x 55 x 55 mm box, so each spool is about 52 mm across the flanges and 23 mm wide.
Six of those need 158.5 mm of axle span, more than a 3-wide crate's 121.5 mm cavity: the
dispenser is 4x2. A 3x2 dispenser fits six spools up to ~16.7 mm wide (see verify()).

families.title: Wall rail
families.summary: A French cleat and shelves that hang crates on the wall above the bench.
families.description:
Wall rail: crates hang on the wall above the bench on a 45 deg French cleat.

Two parts:
- Wall cleat: a strip screwed to the wall, top bevelled at 45 deg so it falls toward the
  wall (the classic French cleat). 10 mm thick, 30 mm tall at its front face, 20 mm at the
  wall face. 4 mm wood screws on a 42 mm pitch (one per grid cell), 90 deg countersinks
  on the front face. Length is `n * 42 - 0.5` so strips butt end to end on the grid.
- Shelf: a tray whose top is a grid of per-cell stacking lips (core `lip_pocket`, one per
  42 mm cell, like a baseplate), so any crate footprint seats on it exactly as it seats on
  another crate. Behind and below the tray: a hook with the matching 45 deg bevel, a back
  plate, a bumper that rests on the wall, and a diagonal brace up to the tray front.

Side profile (wall frame: `u` = distance from the wall face, `z` = up, 0 = cleat bottom).
The shelf back (tray, hook tip and bumper) is flat at `u = 0`. The hook rests on the cleat
bevel; a 0.5 mm gap separates the back plate from the cleat's front face.

Tipping: the crates' centre of mass sits `d = depth / 2` in front of the wall. The cleat
pushes the hook up and toward the wall with equal components, and the bumper pushes back
at a lever `L` below the cleat contact. Without friction the shelf stays hooked while
`L >= d`; the bumper is placed at `L = 1.25 d` (and always low enough that lifting the
shelf 10 mm to unhook it does not hit the cleat).

Loads (assumed): a full 2x2x6 crate is 0.5-1 kg; design load 2 kg per shelf (two full
crates stacked), PETG, E ~ 2 GPa. At 2 kg the bumper and hook forces are ~16-20 N, spread
over the full shelf width: stresses stay well under 1 MPa, so walls are sized for stiffness,
impact and printability (>= 2.4 mm), not strength. The weak links are the wall screws and
anchors. PETG/ASA rather than PLA because PLA creeps under a sustained load.

Printing: the shelf is a constant side profile extruded across its width, so it prints on
its side (an end face on the bed) with no supports and the bending loads lie in the layer
planes. The only overhangs are the lip pockets' end walls facing up the print: 45 deg
chamfers and a 1.8 mm ledge, bridged across the pocket.

families.title: Calibration
families.summary: Small test prints that pick the lip clearance and divider fit for your printer.
families.description:
Calibration coupons: a small, cheap test print that picks the tolerances for YOUR printer.

Parts:
- Lip coupons: 1x1x2 boxes (the shortest box the system allows), one per value in
  CLEARANCES, with the clearance in hundredths of a mm debossed on the front ("25" = 0.25).
  Every optional box feature is off and the floor has a window, to save filament and time.
- Probe: a plain default 1x1x2 box; its feet are the gauge tried in every coupon.
- Slot strip: an L of crate wall with a core divider slot in an X wall and in a Y wall.
- Slot samples: a comb of divider ends (the 1.2 mm plate, then the thick-end candidates)
  printed flat like the real dividers, each finger labelled with its thickness.

Lower limit: a foot's vertical face sits 2.15 mm in from the cell outline and the wall is
2.0 mm thick, so below 0.15 mm of lip clearance the cavity wall, not the lip, sets the play.

Rerun with other values: `uv run python -m stakee.modules.calibration --clearances 0.2 0.3`.
